# Kernels for subgroups generated by Coxeter lifts

Author: Worker 1746.

This internal group-theoretic unit proves a kernel criterion for lifts of the
simple generators of a Coxeter group. Its provenance is the universal property
of a Coxeter presentation and elementary subgroup closure, as implemented by
Mathlib's `CoxeterSystem.lift`, `CoxeterSystem.ext_simple` and quotient groups.
No algebraic-group structure or structural existence theorem is asserted here.

Let `N` and `W` be groups, with independent universes, and let `cs` be a Coxeter
system on `W` with labels `B` and Coxeter matrix `M`. Let `H` be a normal subgroup
of `N` and `m : B → N` any family. The definition `generatedBy H m` is the
subgroup `H ⊔ closure (range m)` of `N`.

The construction `sectionHom` takes the explicit premise that the images of
`m` in `N/H` satisfy all Coxeter relations:
`((m a mod H) * (m b mod H)) ^ M a b = 1` for every `a,b`.
It applies `cs.lift` and hence takes each simple reflection to the corresponding
image of `m a`.

Suppose also that `q : N →* W` sends `m a` to `cs.simple a` and kills `H`.
Then `q` factors through `N/H`. The composite with `sectionHom` agrees with the
identity on each simple reflection, so `cs.ext_simple` proves that it is the
identity on all of `W`. This is `projection_sectionHom`.

The image of `sectionHom` contains the quotient image of `H` because that
image is trivial; it contains the quotient image of every `m a` by the simple
reflection formula. Subgroup closure thus puts the quotient image of
`generatedBy H m` inside that range. For an element of this generated subgroup
lying in `ker q`, choose a preimage `w` in the range. The left inverse formula
forces `w = 1`, so the original element is in `H`. The opposite inclusion uses
`H ≤ ker q`. Thus `generatedBy_inf_ker_eq` proves the equality
`generatedBy H m ⊓ ker q = H`.

For the intended root-generated centralizer application, `N` will be the
actual rational normalizer, `W` its centralizer quotient, and `H` the normal
subgroup generated by the rank-one centralizer intersections. This unit
retains the Coxeter system, the chosen simple lifts and all their relations
modulo `H` as explicit premises. Constructing those data from the actual
algebraic groups remains a separate obligation. This unit alone proves no
unconditional algebraic-group statement.
